question.text: The centres of two circles <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi>C</mi><mn>1</mn></msub></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi>C</mi><mn>2</mn></msub></math> each of unit radius are at a distance of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>6</mn></math> units from each other. Let <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>P</mi></math> be the midpoint of the line segment joining the centres of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi>C</mi><mn>1</mn></msub></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi>C</mi><mn>2</mn></msub></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>C</mi></math> be a circle touching circles <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi>C</mi><mn>1</mn></msub></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi>C</mi><mn>2</mn></msub></math> externally. If a common tangent to <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi>C</mi><mn>1</mn></msub></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>C</mi></math> passing through <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>P</mi></math> is also a common tangent to <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi>C</mi><mn>2</mn></msub></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>C</mi></math>, then the radius (in units) of the circle <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>C</mi></math> is

solution.text:
In  Δ CPC 2 , r + 1 2 = α 2 + 3 2         ...(i)


In Δ PTC , 

α 2 = r 2 + 3 2 - 1 2

α 2 = r 2 + 8

Putting the value of α 2  in equation (i), we get, 

1 + r 2 + 2 r = 1 r 2 + 8 + 9

⇒2r=16⇒r=8
